title: FNV-1a, the address function — 12 machine-checked theorems of the ℤ/9 vortex deposit and how they are bound
description:
FNV-1a, the address function — 12 machine-checked theorems of the ℤ/9 vortex deposit, one Lean namespace, wing the address. 12 close by exhaustion over a finite domain (by decide); 1 rfl declaration(s) are listed and not sealed, by design. Every one is sealed live in the append-only ledger.

How these theorems are bound. "Entangled" is used in this deposit's honest sense: correlation by derivation, not quantum entanglement, and no information travels through it.

1 · Shared definitions. 1 definition(s) are used by two or more theorems, binding 66 pair(s); the theorems fall into 1 strand(s), the largest of 12. Most binding: hash32 (12).

2 · Imports. Built on: no other cluster. Built on it: address.lean, nim.lean, sequences.lean. Checking this cluster needs 1 file(s): src/proof/fnv.lean.

3 · The joint address. The 12 sealed receipts fold to 4f060cb7-40aa-8d0f-a756-a18a83e19033. Order-invariant: yes — the same root in reverse order. Altering one receipt changes it: yes, computed on this run. A content-address proves integrity, not truth.

4 · The address lattice. Each theorem sits at the seven ray values its page plots from its receipt, taken mod 9: a point of (ℤ/9)⁷. This cluster's centre is (7, 5, 4, 4, 8, 2, 3). Its nearest clusters, ranked by lift — pairs observed among each theorem's seven nearest points, over the pairs expected by chance from the two clusters' sizes: demand.lean (4 observed, 1.06 expected, lift 3.76), involution.lean (3 observed, 1.06 expected, lift 2.82), index.lean (3 observed, 1.46 expected, lift 2.05). A lift near 1 is what chance gives. Mean distance between two of its theorems: 14.94; from one of its theorems to a theorem of another cluster: 15.52. A receipt is a hash, so nearness on this lattice is a property of the addresses, not of the mathematics; the mathematical binding is (1) and (2). Chance, measured: over 200 reshufflings of which cluster each point belongs to (seeded, so every rebuild gives the same numbers), a best lift at least this high arose in 28.0% of them — consistent with chance.

Prior art. FNV-1a — Glenn Fowler, Landon Curt Noll and Phong Vo, 1991 Per-theorem prior-art searches — OEIS, zbMATH Open, OpenAlex, Crossref, arXiv — are recorded, with what was searched, where and when, in the living ledger src/proof/novelty.json. No novelty is claimed here.
